Class ProxyProtocolHandler

java.lang.Object
io.netty.channel.ChannelHandlerAdapter
io.netty.channel.ChannelInboundHandlerAdapter
io.micronaut.http.server.netty.handler.ProxyProtocolHandler
All Implemented Interfaces:
io.netty.channel.ChannelHandler, io.netty.channel.ChannelInboundHandler
@Internal public final class ProxyProtocolHandler extends io.netty.channel.ChannelInboundHandlerAdapter
Reads the PROXY protocol (version 1 or 2) header at the start of a connection, records the addresses it carries on the connection channel, and then removes itself. The decoder removes itself too. A connection that does not start with a valid header, or does not send it in time, is closed: falling back to the socket address would let a client that reaches the listener directly choose whether its address is trusted.
Since:
5.3.0

  • Method Details

    • insert

      public static void insert(io.netty.channel.ChannelPipeline pipeline, long timeoutMillis)
      Add the decoder and this handler at the end of the given pipeline. They must come before any other handler that reads the connection, the TLS handler in particular.
      Parameters:
      pipeline - The connection pipeline
      timeoutMillis - How long the peer may take to send the header, <= 0 for no limit

    • insert

      public static void insert(io.netty.channel.ChannelPipeline pipeline, long timeoutMillis, @Nullable Consumer<io.netty.channel.ChannelHandlerContext> afterHeader)
      Add the decoder and this handler at the end of the given pipeline. They must come before any other handler that reads the connection, the TLS handler in particular.
      Parameters:
      pipeline - The connection pipeline
      timeoutMillis - How long the peer may take to send the header, <= 0 for no limit
      afterHeader - Runs once the header is read, before this handler removes itself, with the context of this handler. The bytes that follow the header go to the handlers it adds right after that context.

    • find

      public static @Nullable ProxyProtocolHandler.ProxiedAddresses find(@Nullable io.netty.channel.Channel channel)
      The addresses that the PROXY protocol header of the connection of the given channel carries. The channel may be the connection channel or a stream channel of it.
      Parameters:
      channel - The channel
      Returns:
      The addresses, or null if the connection did not send any (no PROXY protocol, a LOCAL command or an unknown or non-IP protocol)
